note: Sentences that CANNOT be fixed by field edits: a jp re-author requires a new token array (re-run the SudachiPy dissection), and verifier-rejected resolutions need a fresh pass. Deferred - not part of this apply.

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 味噌汁 (みそしる) is a lexicalized compound; 味噌の汁 is not what natives say for the dish, and the explanation compounds the damage by teaching the の link as the grammar point. Since gen=true the jp may be re-authored, so I fixed jp plus kana, romaji, the literal and both explanations in one pass; the token list still shows 味噌/の/汁 and must be re-parsed from the new jp downstream, since token surface forms are not an editable path here.

proposed_edits.new: 朝は味噌汁を飲みます
あさわみそしるをのみます
asawamisoshiruonomimasu

は marks 朝 ('morning') as the topic (the setting being talked about), and を marks 味噌汁 ('miso soup') as the object of 飲む ('to drink/to have'). 味噌汁 is a fixed compound (味噌 'miso' + 汁 'broth'), written with no の between the two parts. 飲みます is the polite present/habitual form. The vocabulary focus is 味噌 ('miso'). In Japanese, soup is 'drunk' (飲む), which is why we use 'to have' in English.

は marca 朝 ('manhã') como o tópico (o cenário sobre o qual se fala), e を marca 味噌汁 ('sopa de missô') como objeto de 飲む ('beber/tomar'). 味噌汁 é um composto fixo (味噌 'missô' + 汁 'caldo'), escrito sem nenhum の entre as duas partes. 飲みます é a forma polida no presente/habitual. O foco do vocabulário é 味噌 ('missô'). Em japonês, sopa se 'bebe' (飲む), por isso usamos 'tomar' em pt-BR.
As for the morning (は), miso soup (を), I drink (polite form).
Quanto à manhã (は), sopa de missô (を), tomo (forma polida).

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 背が痛い is not idiomatic: in modern usage bare 背 reads as stature (背が高い), and back pain is 背中が痛い (or 腰が痛い). gen=true, so jp is re-authorable; I updated jp, kana, romaji, the token reading, and both explanations, which quote 背がいたい verbatim. Token surface 背 → 背中 is outside my editable paths and must follow in the same apply step.

proposed_edits.new: 背中がいたいので病院に行く
せなかがいたいのでびょういんにいく
senakagaitainodebyouinniiku
せなか
senaka

The sentence chains a cause and a consequence using ので ('because/since'). The first part 背中がいたい ('my back hurts') is the reason; the second 病院に行く ('I am going to the hospital') is the result. The parser split ので into の + で, but it functions as a single unit: the causal conjunction ので, which links the two ideas naturally and a little more softly than から.

A frase encadeia uma causa e uma consequência usando ので ('porque/como'). A primeira parte 背中がいたい ('as costas doem') é o motivo; a segunda 病院に行く ('vou ao hospital') é o resultado. O analisador separou ので em の + で, mas funciona como uma unidade só: a conjunção causal ので, que liga as duas ideias de forma natural e um pouco mais suave que から.

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 然うして is an ateji/literary spelling that modern Japanese writes in kana (そうして/そして); keeping it in an N3 teaching sentence is misleading orthography. Reading is unchanged (そう), so kana/romaji and the token readings stay valid; only jp and the explanations that quoted the kanji needed updating (the token surface 然う will be regenerated by re-tokenization of the new jp).

proposed_edits.new: お金をためて、そうして車を買った

The sentence has two actions linked in sequence. The first, お金をためて (to save money), is in the て form, which here indicates 'I did this, and...'. Then comes そうして ('and so / and then'), reinforcing the idea of consequence, and finally 車を買った (I bought a car), in the past. The focus is the word ためる ('to save/set aside money') within a chain of actions.

A frase tem duas ações ligadas em sequência. A primeira, お金をためて (juntar dinheiro), está na forma て, que aqui indica 'fiz isto, e...'. Depois vem そうして ('e aí / e então'), reforçando a ideia de consequência, e finalmente 車を買った (comprei um carro), no passado. O foco é o vocábulo ためる ('juntar/economizar') dentro de uma cadeia de ações.

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: In pt-BR a 'loja' does not serve food, so 'Aquela loja não é barata, mas a comida é gostosa' is incoherent; 店 in this context (cheap/tasty) is an eatery, which is also how the en renders it. The lexical gloss 'loja' stays on the token and in the literal, where the word-level meaning belongs. Same edit set also repairs a corruption I found while resolving: the stray half-width space in jp had been tokenized as a 記号 symbol and its reading leaked into kana/romaji as きごう/kigou, so the space is removed from jp and kana/romaji/token 7 are cleaned.

proposed_edits.new: Aquele restaurante não é barato, mas a comida é gostosa.
あの店は安くはないがおいしい
あのみせわやすくわないがおいしい
anomisewayasukuwanaigaoishii

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: With the pure existence verb いる the location is marked by に (狭い駅に人がたくさんいる); で marks the place of an action or event, so で+いる here is ungrammatical for plain existence. The reading change cascades to kana, romaji and the token's r/romaji.

狭い is 'cramped/narrow', not 'crowded' (混んでいる), and the JP carries no demonstrative, so 'this' was invented. The pt translation carried the same invented deictic ('nesta'), so it is aligned in the same edit set.
The old text taught a false grammar fact (で as the marker of place of existence); with the corrected jp the explanation must state that に marks where something exists with いる/ある.
Same false claim in Portuguese, and it is the learner-facing locale, so it gets the identical correction to に.

proposed_edits.new: 狭い駅に人がたくさんいる
せまいえきにひとがたくさんいる
semaiekinihitogatakusaniru
に
ni
There are a lot of people in the cramped station.
Tem muita gente na estação apertada.

狭い駅 is an i-adjective directly modifying the following noun: 'cramped station'. The particle に marks the place where something exists (used with いる/ある). 人がたくさんいる says that 'many people exist', with いる being the verb of existence for living beings and たくさん the adverb of quantity.

狭い駅 é um adjetivo-i modificando diretamente o substantivo seguinte: 'estação apertada'. A partícula に marca o lugar onde algo existe (usada com いる/ある). 人がたくさんいる diz que 'muita gente existe', com いる sendo o verbo de existência para seres vivos e たくさん o advérbio de quantidade.

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 此処 is a non-jōyō ateji spelling; modern Japanese and every teaching material write ここ in kana, so the orthography is implausible for a course sentence at any level. The reading is unchanged, so only jp and the two explanations that quote 此処は need editing (kana/romaji already read koko).

proposed_edits.new: ここはとても静かだ

Sentence of the type 「X は Y だ」, which describes the topic. ここは establishes the topic (this place), とても is an intensity adverb (very), and 静か is a na-adjective (形状詞) meaning silent/quiet. The だ at the end is the casual copula "is", giving the sentence an informal tone.

Frase do tipo 「X は Y だ」, que descreve o tópico. ここは estabelece o tópico (este lugar), とても é um advérbio de intensidade (muito) e 静か é um adjetivo な (形状詞) que significa silencioso/tranquilo. O だ no final é a cópula casual "é", dando à frase um tom informal.

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 絵を描く is the standard orthography; leaving the easy kanji 絵 in kana while keeping the much harder 描 is inconsistent and creates a genuine ambiguity with the interjection え. Kana and romaji are unaffected since 絵 reads え.

The note is internal pipeline commentary about the tokenizer and does not belong in learner-facing text. With jp re-authored to 絵 the caveat is moot, so it is deleted outright and the を clause now cites 絵 directly.
Same leak in pt-BR ('o tokenizador rotulou'). Removed, with the を clause pointing straight at 絵 (desenho).

proposed_edits.new: 厚い紙に絵を描いた

The sentence follows the basic Japanese order (complements before the verb, which comes last). 厚い紙 is the い-adjective 厚い (thick) directly modifying the noun 紙 (paper). に marks the place where the action takes hold (on the paper), を marks the direct object 絵 (drawing), and the verb 描く (to draw) comes at the end, in the past form 描いた.

A frase segue a ordem japonesa básica (complementos antes do verbo, que vem por último). 厚い紙 é o adjetivo-i 厚い (grosso) modificando diretamente o substantivo 紙 (papel). に marca o lugar onde a ação se fixa (no papel), を marca o objeto direto 絵 (desenho), e o verbo 描く (desenhar) vem no fim, na forma passada 描いた.
drawing
desenho

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 手の裏 is dictionary-defined as the palm (= 手のひら); the back of the hand is 手の甲, so the sentence flatly contradicts its own en/pt translations. Rewriting the possessor as 紙 keeps the target vocab 裏 in its core 'reverse side' sense and gives a natural request, so kana, romaji, translations, literals, explanation and token 0 are all updated in the same set.
'手の裏 here is tokenized as a single word' is internal pipeline detail, not grammar a learner needs. Dropped, and the explanation re-authored for 紙の裏 with の linking the two nouns.
Same tokenization leak in pt-BR. Dropped and the explanation re-authored for 紙の裏.

proposed_edits.new: 紙の裏を見せてください
かみのうらをみせてください
kaminouraomisetekudasai
Please show me the back of the paper.
Mostre o verso do papel, por favor.
The paper's back, show (it), please.
O verso do papel, mostre, por favor.

The object 紙の裏 ('the back of the paper') is marked by を, and the request is formed with the て-form of the verb 見せる ('to show') + ください ('please'). 紙の裏 links two nouns with の: 裏 (back, reverse side) modified by 紙 (paper). The key word here is 裏.

O objeto 紙の裏 ('o verso do papel') é marcado por を, e o pedido se forma com a forma-て do verbo 見せる ('mostrar') + ください ('por favor'). 紙の裏 liga dois substantivos com の: 裏 (parte de trás, verso) modificado por 紙 (papel). A palavra em foco aqui é 裏.
かみのうら
kaminoura
back of the paper
verso do papel

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 彼女の毛 reads as her body hair or fur; head hair is 髪 or 髪の毛, so the JP contradicts its own translations. Moving the possessor to 猫 keeps the target vocab 毛 in its natural 'fur' sense (replacing 毛 with 髪 would orphan the vocab link), so kana, romaji, translations, literals, explanation and tokens 0 and 2 are updated together.

proposed_edits.new: 猫の毛はとてもきれいだ
ねこのけわとてもきれいだ
nekonokewatotemokireida
The cat's fur is very beautiful.
O pelo do gato é muito bonito.
As for the cat's fur, it is very beautiful.
Quanto ao pelo do gato, (é) muito bonito.

Topic + comment: 猫の毛は establishes the theme (the cat's fur) and きれいだ makes the statement. きれい is a な-adjective (nominal adjective), so it uses だ at the end instead of conjugating like an い-adjective. とても reinforces the degree ('very'). The focus is the vocabulary 毛 (fur/hair).

Tópico + comentário: 猫の毛は estabelece o tema (o pelo do gato) e きれいだ faz a afirmação. きれい é um adjetivo-な (adjetivo nominal), por isso usa だ no fim em vez de conjugar como い-adjetivo. とても reforça o grau ('muito'). O foco é o vocabulário 毛 (pelo/cabelo).
ねこ
neko
cat
gato
modificador (dono)
fur, hair
pelo (pelagem)

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 此処 is 表外/literary orthography for ここ; modern native writing and all JLPT-oriented material use the kana form, so it is genuinely unnatural for a learner sentence. Both structure_explanation fields quote 此処に and must cascade; kana and romaji already read ここ and stay unchanged.

proposed_edits.new: ここに座ってもいいですか

Here appears the permission-asking pattern 「verb in te-form + も + いい」 (座ってもいい = may sit / it's okay to sit). ここに marks the place where one wants to sit, 座って is the te-form of the verb, も adds the sense of "even (if)", and いいですか politely asks whether it is okay. Together it becomes the polite request "may I sit here?".

Aqui aparece o padrão de pedir permissão 「verbo na forma て + も + いい」 (座ってもいい = pode sentar / está ok sentar). O ここに marca o lugar onde se quer sentar, 座って é a forma て do verbo, も acrescenta o sentido de "mesmo (se)", e いいですか pergunta educadamente se está tudo bem. O conjunto vira o pedido cortês "posso me sentar aqui?".

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: Negated existence of an animate noun requires いない; 〜はない with a person survives only in literary set phrases (and then typically with 者), so 学生はない is unnatural modern Japanese. kana, romaji, both explanations (which quote はない three times) and the final token's note all cascade, since ない now negates the verb いる rather than standing alone as the existential.

proposed_edits.new: この問題が解けない学生はいない
このもんだいがとけないがくせいわいない
konomondaigatokenaigakuseiwainai

The sentence uses the target pattern 〜ない〜はいない, a double negation that affirms emphatically: 'there is no X that does not...'. First comes a relative clause この問題が解けない ('that cannot solve this problem') that qualifies the noun 学生 ('student'); then 学生は is the topic and the sentence closes with はいない ('there is none'). Because 学生 is a person, existence is negated with いない (from いる), never with ない. The two negations (解けない and はいない) cancel out and the final meaning is positive and emphatic: every student can solve it.

A frase usa o padrão-alvo 〜ない〜はいない, uma dupla negação que afirma de forma enfática: 'não existe X que não...'. Primeiro vem uma oração relativa この問題が解けない ('que não consegue resolver este problema') que qualifica o substantivo 学生 ('estudante'); depois 学生は é o tópico e a frase fecha com はいない ('não existe'). Como 学生 é pessoa, a existência se nega com いない (de いる), nunca com ない. As duas negações (解けない e はいない) se cancelam e o sentido final é positivo e enfático: todo estudante consegue resolvê-lo.
ない here negates the verb いる: いない denies the existence of animate beings (people)
aqui ない nega o verbo いる: いない nega a existência de seres animados (pessoas)

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: Bare declarative 〜たい is restricted to the speaker (or questions); a third-person subject requires 〜たがる/evidential marking, so 妹はピアノを習いたい teaches a wrong pattern. The recast to 私 keeps the 〜たい teaching target, the topic-は structure and the token count intact (no vocab is declared as the target in the explanation, unlike the お兄さん record), whereas 習いたがっている would silently retarget the whole record.

proposed_edits.new: 私はピアノを習いたい
わたしわぴあのをならいたい
watashiwapianoonaraitai
I want to learn the piano.
Quero aprender piano.
As for me, I want to learn piano.
Quanto a mim, piano (objeto), quero aprender.

Topic 私は (I) + object ピアノを (piano) + verb in the desiderative 習いたい (want to learn). The 〜たい is formed with the conjunctive stem of the verb (習い) plus the auxiliary たい, which expresses the speaker's own desire; to state a third person's wish you use 〜たがる instead (妹はピアノを習いたがっている). The sentence is casual (ending in たい, without です), so the translation is in a neutral register.

Tópico 私は (eu) + objeto ピアノを (piano) + verbo no desiderativo 習いたい (quero aprender). O 〜たい se forma com a raiz conjuntiva do verbo (習い) mais o auxiliar たい, que exprime o desejo do próprio falante; para afirmar o desejo de outra pessoa, usa-se 〜たがる (妹はピアノを習いたがっている). A frase é casual (termina em たい, sem です), então a tradução fica num registro neutro.
わたし
watashi
I
eu

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: 輸入する already means bringing goods INTO the country, so 外国に輸入する is contradictory; the origin is marked with から (外国から輸入する). Every other field (en, pt, lit_en) already says 'from abroad', so the Japanese was the odd one out.
'para o exterior' mirrored the broken に and contradicted the natural pt and both en fields. With から the literal must mirror origin: 'do exterior'.

proposed_edits.new: 車を外国から輸入する会社です
くるまをがいこくからゆにゅうするかいしゃです
kurumaogaikokukarayunyuusurukaishadesu
Carro (objeto) do exterior importar empresa é.

The sentence has a relative clause: 車を外国から輸入する ('to import cars from abroad') comes directly before the noun 会社 ('company') and modifies it, with no particle between them. The verb 輸入する ('to import') is in dictionary form because it modifies a noun. The vocabulary focus here is 輸入する ('to import'): note that を marks the imported object (車) and から marks the origin (外国), the place the goods come from. The sentence ends in です, politely closing the structure 'X is a company that...'.

A frase tem uma oração relativa: 車を外国から輸入する ('importar carros do exterior') vem diretamente antes do substantivo 会社 ('empresa') e o modifica, sem partícula entre eles. O verbo 輸入する ('importar') está na forma de dicionário porque modifica um substantivo. O foco de vocabulário aqui é 輸入する ('importar'): note que を marca o objeto importado (車) e から marca a origem (外国), o lugar de onde a mercadoria vem. A frase termina em です, fechando de forma educada a estrutura 'X é uma empresa que...'.
complemento de origem

decisions.why: 以下 is normally written in kanji; bare いか after a quantity is nonstandard orthography and collides with イカ (squid). Both kanji are inside the N5/N4 range and the explanation already cites the kanji form, so the sentence should show it.

proposed_edits.new: このケーキは五百円以下です

sentences.why: jp re-author: needs re-dissection (token surfaces are not field-editable)

decisions.why: お兄さん is the honorific form, reserved for someone else's older brother or for direct address; referring to your own to a third party takes the humble 兄. Since the explanation names お兄さん as the target vocabulary, the fix moves the possessor instead of the noun (友達のお兄さん), which keeps the vocab link, the A は B が 形容詞 pattern and the token count.

proposed_edits.new: 友達のお兄さんは背が高い
ともだちのおにいさんわせがたかい
tomodachinooniisanwasegatakai
My friend's older brother is tall.
O irmão mais velho do meu amigo é alto.
As for my friend's older brother, his height is tall.
Quanto ao irmão mais velho do meu amigo, a estatura é alta.

The sentence uses the classic descriptive structure A は B が 形容詞: the general topic is 友達のお兄さん 'my friend's older brother' (with の of possession), and within it 背 'stature' is marked by が as the specific aspect that is 高い 'tall'. The target is the vocabulary お兄さん, which refers to someone else's older brother; to speak about your own you say 兄. In English we simply say 'is tall', without repeating 'the stature'.

A frase usa a estrutura clássica de descrição A は B が 形容詞: o tópico geral é 友達のお兄さん 'o irmão mais velho do meu amigo' (com の de posse), e dentro dele 背 'estatura' é marcado por が como o aspecto específico que é 高い 'alto'. O alvo é o vocabulário お兄さん, que se usa para o irmão mais velho de outra pessoa; para falar do próprio irmão, diz-se 兄. Em português dizemos simplesmente 'é alto', sem repetir 'a estatura'.
ともだち
tomodachi
friend
amigo
